source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Gynecomastia, a recognized spironolactone adverse effect that warrants assessment and discussion with the prescriber.","B":"Anaphylaxis, because isolated breast enlargement and tenderness are typical manifestations of an acute allergic reaction.","C":"Breast cancer, because new tenderness while taking spironolactone establishes a malignant diagnosis without evaluation.","D":"An unrelated symptom, because spironolactone has no known association with breast enlargement or tenderness in men."}}
source_row.rationale: Gynecomastia and breast tenderness are recognized spironolactone adverse effects and merit medication assessment; the finding alone neither proves allergy nor cancer.
source_row.source_detail: Adverse reactions/warnings: spironolactone can cause gynecomastia; risk is related to dosage level and duration and is usually reversible after discontinuation. DailyMed FDA labeling revised May 2026; rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A male client taking spironolactone develops breast tenderness and enlargement. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
